audit_items.title: Falsification Test: Can a sidecar with tampered column data and invalid KZG proofs be accepted by the gossip validation pipeline?
audit_items.state_context: kzgChan (buffered channel, cap=100) drains into kzgVerifierRoutine; verifyKzgBatch broadcasts same error to all co-batched verifiers; fallback validateUnbatchedColumnsKzg re-runs individual verification when batch fails

phase1.abstract_interpretation: The batch KZG verification pipeline aggregates multiple sidecars from the kzgChan into a flat allDataColumns slice, calls VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs once, and broadcasts the same pass/fail result to all co-batched verifiers. There is no code path allowing a sidecar with an invalid KZG proof to receive ValidationAccept. Batch failure triggers the fallback validateUnbatchedColumnsKzg which re-runs the same cryptographic check on the specific sidecar's columns only — this is mathematically equivalent and cannot produce a false positive. The alleged index semantics bug (sidecar.Index used as cell_index) is NOT a bug: CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB=128 equals NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS=128, and the Fulu spec explicitly maps sidecar.index to cell_index in verify_data_column_sidecar_kzg_proofs.
key_observations: No false positive acceptance possible via batch; cryptographic guarantee from ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch
Batch poisoning causes DoS: one invalid sidecar forces all co-batched sidecars to trigger the slower fallback individual verification path at 2x compute cost
seenDataColumnCache is updated only after ValidationAccept — rejected/ignored sidecars can be resubmitted
sidecar.Index as cell_index is correct per Fulu spec: CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB=NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS=128

phase2.symbolic_execution: Path 1 (attacker alone): validateDataColumn(S_attacker) → ValidFields(pass, structure consistent) → ValidProposerSignature(pass) → SidecarInclusionProven(pass) → validateWithKzgBatchVerifier → kzgVerifierRoutine → verifyKzgBatch → VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs(S_attacker) → VerifyCellKZGProofBatch → (false, nil) → ErrInvalidKZGProof → resChan←err → validateUnbatchedColumnsKzg(S_attacker) → same result → ValidationReject. Path 2 (co-batched): S_attacker + S_honest in same batch → batch fails (S_attacker invalid) → both verifiers get same error → S_attacker fallback→REJECT, S_honest fallback→ACCEPT. No false positive on safety path.
attack_scenarios: Batch poisoning DoS: attacker submits malformed sidecars at high rate; honest sidecars co-batched with invalid ones trigger fallback at 2x compute cost; at sustained attack rates, node throughput is degraded but no incorrect acceptance occurs

Forced replay: since invalid sidecars are not cached in seenDataColumnCache, rejected sidecar can be resubmitted each slot; gossip scoring may eventually penalize peers, but this is external to the KZG verification logic

edge_cases: Zero-length column caught by VerifyDataColumnSidecar ErrMismatchLength before reaching KZG verification
sidecar.Index=127 (max) as cell_index: valid, since ckzg4844 accepts cell indices 0..CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB-1=127
All-zero proofs: ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch returns (false, nil) or (false, error); both paths result in REJECT
phase2_5.timing_dependencies: None that affect safety invariant. Batch timing affects availability (DoS) not correctness.

phase3.invariant_verification: I1 (invalid KZG proof never accepted): HOLDS. Cryptographic guarantee from ckzg4844: batch path → false → ErrInvalidKZGProof → fallback → same result. No code path produces ValidationAccept for invalid proof. Guards are sufficient. I4 (seen-cache does not bypass KZG for rejected sidecars): HOLDS. seenDataColumnCache check occurs after validateWithKzgBatchVerifier; rejection prevents cache entry.
phase3.guard_identified: ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch (C-KZG library) as the mathematical guard; validateUnbatchedColumnsKzg as the fallback guard ensuring safety even when batch verification is poisoned
phase3.guard_sufficiency: Sufficient for safety (no false acceptance). Insufficient for availability (batch poisoning degrades throughput).

scope_filtering.reason: Batch poisoning is an exploitable DoS pattern: one invalid sidecar forces all co-batched verifications to fall back to individual processing, doubling compute. Sustained attack from a single P2P peer degrades node throughput during peak periods. This is low severity but is an externally reachable, exploitable DoS from the P2P entry point.
scope_filtering.severity_estimate: Low (performance/availability DoS via batch poisoning; no safety impact; no false acceptance)

audit_items.reasoning: The core falsification test (CHK-0061) finds no code path by which a sidecar with tampered KZG proofs can be accepted. The KZG proof verification via ckzg4844 is a mathematical gate with no bypass. However, batch poisoning (one invalid sidecar forces all co-batched sidecars to fall back to individual verification) is a real exploitable DoS pattern from the P2P entry point, warranting informational finding with low-severity bug bounty eligibility.
recommendations: Add per-peer rate limiting at the gossip validation layer before KZG verification to reduce batch poisoning impact
Consider adding a negative result cache (slot, proposer_index, column_index → rejected) to prevent unlimited resubmission of rejected sidecars
Instrument kzgChan fill level as a metric to detect active DoS campaigns

audit_items.title: Verify Pre-Condition Ordering: Does KZG proof verification occur after structural and signature validation?
audit_items.state_context: kzgChan buffered channel (capacity 100); kzgVerifierRoutine single goroutine; SecondsPerSlot=12 for timeout; ValidationIgnore path does not update seenDataColumnCache

phase1.abstract_interpretation: The gossip validation pipeline in validateDataColumn correctly orders validation steps: structural checks (ValidFields), subnet checks, time/finalization checks, parent validity, proposer signature, inclusion proof, and THEN KZG proof verification. KZG is explicitly the last REJECT check, consistent with spec ordering for DoS protection (expensive computation last). However, a critical availability vulnerability exists in validateWithKzgBatchVerifier: when the kzgChan is saturated (capacity 100), the 12-second context timeout fires and returns ValidationIgnore rather than ValidationReject. This means invalid sidecars can avoid permanent rejection indefinitely if the verifier queue is maintained at saturation.
key_observations: Validation ordering is CORRECT: structural → signature → KZG (consistent with spec)
KZG verification is computationally expensive and correctly placed last among REJECT checks
CRITICAL: context timeout in validateWithKzgBatchVerifier returns ValidationIgnore, not ValidationReject
Invalid sidecars that time out are not cached in seenDataColumnCache, enabling unlimited resubmission
The fallback validateUnbatchedColumnsKzg inherits the partially-exhausted context, but since ckzg4844 is synchronous and not context-aware, this does not affect correctness

phase2.symbolic_execution: Ordering verification: ValidFields(L81) → CorrectSubnet(L86) → NotFromFutureSlot(L92, IGNORE) → SlotAboveFinalized(L98, IGNORE) → SidecarParentSeen(L104, IGNORE+async) → SidecarParentValid(L117, REJECT) → ValidProposerSignature(L123, REJECT) → SidecarParentSlotLower(L129, REJECT) → SidecarDescendsFromFinalized(L135, REJECT) → SidecarInclusionProven(L141, REJECT) → validateWithKzgBatchVerifier(L148, REJECT/IGNORE). Ordering invariant confirmed as correct. Queue saturation attack: attacker submits 100 structurally valid, signature-valid sidecars rapidly → kzgChan fills to capacity 100 → subsequent legitimate sidecar sends to kzgChan (blocks? No — it will block until space available or context cancels). Actually kzgChan<-verificationSet at L163 is a blocking send with no timeout. If channel is full, the goroutine blocks here. The parent context (from pubsub validation) has a timeout. Goroutine blocks until either channel drains or context expires. ValidationIgnore returned on context expiry.
attack_scenarios: Queue saturation DoS (VERIFIED): Send 100+ structurally valid, properly signed sidecars with invalid KZG proofs rapidly to fill kzgChan. Subsequent legitimate sidecar sends block at `s.kzgChan <- verificationSet`. The pubsub validation context times out. Return ValidationIgnore. Legitimate sidecars are never permanently processed. Attacker maintains pressure across slots.

Replay amplification: Each IGNORE'd sidecar (valid or invalid) can be resubmitted next slot without cost (no negative cache). Combined with queue saturation, attacker achieves indefinite processing denial for specific column indices critical to data availability sampling.

edge_cases: Parallel validation: Multiple goroutines can simultaneously call validateWithKzgBatchVerifier (one per gossip message). Each sends to kzgChan independently. Channel capacity 100 means up to 100 concurrent unprocessed KZG requests. Under heavy legitimate traffic, the channel fills naturally.

Context propagation: The parent context from pubsub has its own deadline (typically per-slot). The 12-second timeout in validateWithKzgBatchVerifier may not be the binding constraint if parent context has a shorter deadline.

Recovery after DoS: Once attacker stops flooding, kzgVerifierRoutine drains the channel. No persistent damage. But during active attack, sustained queue saturation requires only ~100 messages/slot from a single peer.
phase2_5.timing_dependencies: Queue saturation requires maintaining kzgChan fill level > 0 before each legitimate sidecar arrives. With 128 columns per slot and 12-second slots, node normally processes ~10 sidecars/second. Attacker needs to inject at least 10 invalid sidecars/second to saturate. Gossip rate limiting may constrain this, but with multiple colluding peers it is achievable.

phase3.invariant_verification: I2 (KZG after structural/signature): HOLDS. Static analysis of validateDataColumn confirms structural and signature checks precede KZG. DoS-safety invariant: VIOLATED. The availability invariant 'invalid sidecars are eventually and permanently rejected' fails because ValidationIgnore is not final rejection, and there is no mechanism preventing indefinite resubmission of timed-out sidecars. I5 (ValidationIgnore does not cause permanent acceptance): HOLDS for correctness (ignored sidecar is not stored). FAILS for availability (ignored sidecar can be resubmitted).
phase3.proof_failure_reason: The DoS availability invariant fails: validateWithKzgBatchVerifier's timeout path returns ValidationIgnore, not ValidationReject, for invalid sidecars when the verifier queue is saturated. No negative result cache prevents unlimited replay.
phase3.guard_identified: validateWithKzgBatchVerifier context timeout (12 seconds) as liveness guard — INSUFFICIENT for availability
phase3.guard_sufficiency: Sufficient for correctness (no false acceptance). INSUFFICIENT for availability (ValidationIgnore enables indefinite resubmission under queue saturation).

scope_filtering.reason: Queue saturation DoS exploiting validateWithKzgBatchVerifier's ValidationIgnore timeout path is externally reachable from P2P gossip. An attacker maintaining ~100 concurrent pending KZG requests can cause legitimate data column sidecar verifications to return ValidationIgnore instead of being processed. Since PeerDAS data availability sampling depends on receiving and verifying a sufficient number of data columns per slot, sustained interference with column verification directly degrades data availability for the node, with downstream effects on block processing.
scope_filtering.severity_estimate: Medium (externally reachable, quantifiable DoS impact on data availability sampling; no safety impact; requires sustained effort from attacker)

audit_items.reasoning: The pre-condition ordering invariant (structural → signature → KZG) is correctly implemented and verified. However, the KZG verification timeout path (ValidationIgnore) creates a real availability vulnerability: an attacker maintaining kzgChan saturation at ~100 concurrent requests causes legitimate sidecar verifications to time out and return ValidationIgnore. Since timed-out sidecars are not cached in the seen-datacolumn cache, they can be resubmitted indefinitely. This directly impacts PeerDAS data availability sampling. Bug bounty eligible at Medium severity.
recommendations: Add rate limiting per peer-ID at the gossip ingress layer to limit the rate of sidecars reaching KZG verification
Increase kzgChan buffer capacity based on expected concurrent validation load, or implement back-pressure signaling
Add a negative result cache (slot, proposer_index, column_index → rejected) to prevent resubmission after initial rejection
Consider using ValidationReject instead of ValidationIgnore on timeout for proven-structurally-valid sidecars that time out, after sufficient DoS protections are in place
Separate the kzgChan timeout from the parent gossip context to ensure KZG always completes or explicitly rejects, never silently ignores

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-001/tb-002/tb-003: Does bytes_to_bls_field reject integers >= BLS_MODULUS?
audit_items.state_context: The Go kzg wrapper delegates entirely to ckzg4844 C library. No application-layer bytes_to_bls_field implementation exists in Go. Trust boundary: Go application layer trusts C-KZG library for all cryptographic validation including field element range checking.

phase1.abstract_interpretation: There is no explicit Go-level implementation of bytes_to_bls_field or field element range validation (< BLS_MODULUS). The Cell type is simply `[BytesPerCell]byte` — a raw byte array. When cells are passed to `ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch`, the C-KZG library performs deserialization of cells into field elements, which includes the mandatory range check per the EIP-7594 specification. If a cell contains bytes representing a value >= BLS_MODULUS, the library returns either `(false, error)` or `(false, nil)`. Both cases result in ErrInvalidKZGProof or the error being returned, causing ValidationReject.
key_observations: No Go-layer bytes_to_bls_field implementation; range check entirely delegated to C-KZG library
C-KZG library (github.com/ethereum/c-kzg-4844/v2) is EIP-4844/EIP-7594 reference implementation
Both error return and false return from ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch result in rejection
Cell type is an opaque byte array [BytesPerCell]byte with no type-level invariant enforcement in Go

phase2.symbolic_execution: Attack: attacker sends cell where bytes 0..31 represent value V >= BLS_MODULUS (e.g., V = BLS_MODULUS = 52435875175126190479447740508185965837690552500527637822603658699938581184513). Path: validateDataColumn → ... → validateWithKzgBatchVerifier → verifyKzgBatch → VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs → kzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch(commitments, [idx], [cell_with_V_>=_modulus], proofs) → ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch → C library deserializes cell: field element V >= BLS_MODULUS → returns (false, error) or (false, nil) → Go wrapper returns error or (false, nil) → VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs returns error or ErrInvalidKZGProof → ValidationReject. ATTACK FAILS: sidecar is correctly rejected by the C-KZG library.
attack_scenarios: Boundary value test: V = BLS_MODULUS (exact) — C library should reject as out-of-range
V = BLS_MODULUS - 1 — should be accepted as valid field element
V = 2^256-1 (all-ones) — should be rejected as far out of range
All cases handled correctly by C-KZG library; no Go-level mitigation needed or available

edge_cases: C-KZG library version mismatch: if a different version with a bug is linked, the field element check could fail; no defense in depth at Go layer
CGO boundary: data is passed as byte arrays via CGO; no serialization corruption possible for fixed-size arrays
All-zero cell: a cell of all zeros does NOT necessarily represent a valid field element in all contexts; C library validates
phase2_5.timing_dependencies: None. The C library check is synchronous within the same batch verification call.

phase3.invariant_verification: I3 (field elements validated < BLS_MODULUS): CONDITIONALLY HOLDS. The validation exists and is performed, but exclusively within the C-KZG library. If the library is correct (which it is for the audited version, github.com/ethereum/c-kzg-4844/v2), the invariant holds. No Go-level defense-in-depth exists. The trust boundary (tb-001/tb-002/tb-003) is correctly identified: Go application trusts C-KZG for all field arithmetic including range validation.
phase3.guard_identified: ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch (C-KZG library) performing bytes_to_bls_field internally during cell deserialization
phase3.guard_sufficiency: Sufficient given trust in the C-KZG library. Insufficient for defense-in-depth (no Go-layer fallback if library has a regression).

scope_filtering.reason: The field element range validation is correctly performed by the C-KZG library. The Go code correctly delegates to this established, well-audited cryptographic dependency. The absence of a Go-level bytes_to_bls_field check is an acceptable architectural decision — adding a redundant Go-level check would duplicate computation without meaningful security benefit given the library's track record. The C-KZG library is the reference implementation for EIP-4844/EIP-7594 and is audited separately. This finding does not constitute a vulnerability in the audited Go codebase.

audit_items.reasoning: BLS field element range validation (bytes_to_bls_field, value < BLS_MODULUS) is correctly performed by the C-KZG library (ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch). No Go-level explicit check exists, but this is an acceptable trust delegation to a well-audited cryptographic reference implementation. Invalid field elements (>= BLS_MODULUS) result in rejection via error return from the C library. No code path allows acceptance of cells with out-of-range field elements through the audited code paths.
recommendations: Consider adding application-layer bounds checking on cell data as defense-in-depth against future C-KZG library regressions
Ensure C-KZG library version is pinned and reviewed during dependency updates
Add test cases with boundary field elements (BLS_MODULUS-1, BLS_MODULUS, BLS_MODULUS+1) to the test suite to verify C library behavior

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Is range validation enforced when actor-blob-submitter sends type-3 transactions with blob data?
audit_items.state_context: Type-3 transaction validation occurs at execution layer (not in scope for beacon chain code). Beacon chain receives KZG commitments in SignedBeaconBlock.Body. Data column sidecars are produced from blobs and propagated via P2P. The C-KZG library handles cell-level field element range checking during proof verification.

phase1.abstract_interpretation: The check asks whether type-3 transaction blob data is validated for field element range (< BLS_MODULUS) before entering the beacon chain pipeline. The beacon chain code (prysm) does not directly process type-3 transactions — this is the responsibility of the execution client (EL). The consensus layer receives KZG commitments via the ExecutionPayload and verifies them using BlobToKZGCommitment/VerifyCellKZGProofBatch. For data column sidecars specifically, cells are received via P2P gossip and validated by VerifyCellKZGProofBatch, which internally performs field element validation via the C-KZG library. The transaction submission path (blob submission via EIP-4844 type-3 tx) is out of scope for the beacon chain code; the execution layer validates blob structure including field element range.
key_observations: Type-3 transaction blob validation is out-of-scope for beacon chain (prysm) code; this is execution layer responsibility
Beacon chain validates cells/columns received via P2P through VerifyCellKZGProofBatch
The C-KZG library enforces BLS_MODULUS constraint during cell deserialization within proof verification
No direct transaction processing code in beacon chain for type-3 transactions

phase2.symbolic_execution: Transaction submission path: actor-blob-submitter → type-3 tx → execution client mempool → EL validates blob commitments/proofs → EL propagates to beacon node via Engine API → beacon node includes in block proposal → signed block body contains KZG commitments. At no point does the beacon chain code process raw blob bytes from type-3 transactions directly. The beacon chain only processes cells (derived blobs) received via P2P gossip, where VerifyCellKZGProofBatch handles field element validation. An attacker submitting a type-3 tx with bytes >= BLS_MODULUS would be rejected by the execution client's blob validation, not the beacon chain code.
attack_scenarios: Out-of-scope attack: attacker submits type-3 tx with V >= BLS_MODULUS → execution client rejects at mempool insertion (execution layer responsibility)
In-scope scenario: attacker sends crafted data column sidecar via gossip with cells containing V >= BLS_MODULUS → handled by CHK-0065 analysis (P2P path)

edge_cases: The check cannot be validated in isolation from the execution client; beacon chain code assumes execution layer has performed blob validation before including commitments in blocks
EIP-4844 specifies that commitments must be valid before inclusion; execution clients validate this

phase3.invariant_verification: The invariant 'type-3 transaction blobs with V >= BLS_MODULUS are rejected before entering the beacon chain' relies on the execution layer's validation. Within the beacon chain code (the audited scope), there is no direct processing of type-3 transaction blob bytes. The C-KZG library provides the final cryptographic gate for any cells/commitments that reach the consensus layer via P2P.
phase3.guard_identified: Execution layer blob validation (out of scope); C-KZG library for cells received via P2P
phase3.guard_sufficiency: Sufficient within the beacon chain code scope. The architectural boundary between execution layer and consensus layer is the trust boundary here.

scope_filtering.reason: The check targets type-3 transaction validation which is out of scope for the beacon chain (prysm) code. The execution client is responsible for validating blob field elements before they become KZG commitments in signed blocks. Within the beacon chain code, cells received via P2P are validated by the C-KZG library which correctly enforces BLS_MODULUS bounds. No gap exists in the audited code.

audit_items.reasoning: Type-3 transaction blob validation (including field element range checking) is the responsibility of the execution client, not the beacon chain. The beacon chain (prysm) receives KZG commitments from the execution layer after execution-layer validation. For cells received via P2P, the C-KZG library performs the field element range check. No code path in the audited beacon chain code allows cells with V >= BLS_MODULUS to be accepted — they would fail ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch. The check scope is split between execution layer (out of scope) and beacon chain (covered by C-KZG).
recommendations: Ensure integration tests cover the full path from type-3 transaction submission through to data column sidecar gossip validation to confirm end-to-end field element validation
Document the execution layer / consensus layer trust boundary for blob validation clearly in the codebase

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Is range validation enforced when actor-p2p-peer receives cells via gossip or RPC?
audit_items.state_context: Two P2P paths: (1) Gossip via validateDataColumn with kzgVerifierRoutine batching and 12-second timeout; (2) RPC ByRoot/ByRange via direct SidecarKzgProofVerified call. Both paths ultimately reach ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch which enforces field element range constraints.

phase1.abstract_interpretation: Both P2P gossip and RPC paths for receiving data column sidecars containing cells reach VerifyCellKZGProofBatch, which delegates to the C-KZG library. The library internally performs bytes_to_bls_field deserialization with range checking during proof verification. There is no Go-level explicit field element validation, but both paths are covered by the C library. The gossip path has the additional complexity of batch verification with a timeout, while the RPC path is synchronous and direct. Both correctly reject cells with V >= BLS_MODULUS.
key_observations: Gossip path: validateDataColumn → validateWithKzgBatchVerifier → verifyKzgBatch → VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs → VerifyCellKZGProofBatch → C-KZG (field element range check)
RPC path: SidecarKzgProofVerified → verifyDataColumnsCommitment → VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs → VerifyCellKZGProofBatch → C-KZG (field element range check)
RPC path is SAFER: synchronous, no timeout path, no ValidationIgnore escape hatch
Gossip path has DoS vector (queue saturation → ValidationIgnore) identified in CHK-0062, but this does not affect field element range validation correctness
Peer scoring for invalid sidecars: gossip scoring may not heavily penalize peers that trigger ValidationIgnore (vs ValidationReject), reducing deterrence

phase2.symbolic_execution: Attack: P2P peer sends DataColumnSidecar via gossip where sidecar.Column[i] contains bytes representing field element V >= BLS_MODULUS. Path: Gossip received → validateDataColumn → ValidFields (pass: structure is consistent) → ... → SidecarInclusionProven (pass: attacker has valid header/inclusion proof) → validateWithKzgBatchVerifier → verifyKzgBatch → VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs → kzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch(commitments, [idx], [cell_with_V>=modulus], proofs) → ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch: C library deserializes cells, finds V >= BLS_MODULUS → returns (false, error) → VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs returns wrapped error → verificationErr set → all resChan receivers get error → validateUnbatchedColumnsKzg fallback → same result → ValidationReject. ATTACK FAILS for safety. RPC path: same VerifyCellKZGProofBatch call → C library rejects → error returned → RPC handler rejects sidecar.
attack_scenarios: Direct cell manipulation: attacker modifies cells after computing valid proofs (proofs become invalid for modified cells); rejected by KZG proof verification
Invalid field element submission: attacker sends cells where bytes >= BLS_MODULUS; rejected by C-KZG library during deserialization within VerifyCellKZGProofBatch
Subtle attack: attacker computes 'valid' proofs for cells with V = BLS_MODULUS-1 (largest valid field element); this is valid and would be accepted (correct behavior)

edge_cases: ByRoot RPC path calls VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs directly without the batch verifier timeout; this is SAFER than the gossip path — no ValidationIgnore escape hatch
ByRange RPC path: same synchronous path as ByRoot

Gossip vs RPC inconsistency: gossip can return ValidationIgnore for valid sidecars under load (DoS), but RPC always returns a definitive pass/fail. This inconsistency means node's data availability sampling may degrade differently for gossip vs. RPC sourced columns.

Peer scoring: a peer sending sidecars with V >= BLS_MODULUS via gossip receives ValidationReject, triggering negative gossip scoring (correct deterrence). A peer causing ValidationIgnore via queue saturation receives no scoring penalty.
phase2_5.timing_dependencies: Queue saturation DoS (CHK-0062) applies to gossip path only. RPC path is not affected by kzgChan saturation.

phase3.invariant_verification: I3 (field elements validated < BLS_MODULUS on P2P receipt): HOLDS for both gossip and RPC paths. The C-KZG library performs the range check in VerifyCellKZGProofBatch for all P2P received cells. The guard is applied consistently. No code path allows cells with V >= BLS_MODULUS to be stored or used. The gossip path DoS (CHK-0062) does not affect the correctness of this invariant — timed-out sidecars are IGNORED (not accepted), and on retry they still face the same cryptographic gate.
phase3.guard_identified: ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch (C-KZG library) applied on both gossip and RPC paths via VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs
phase3.guard_sufficiency: Sufficient for correctness. Both paths uniformly apply the C-KZG library check. RPC path is more conservative (no timeout/IGNORE path). Gossip path has the availability concern (CHK-0062) but not a correctness gap.

scope_filtering.reason: Field element range validation for P2P received cells is correctly enforced by the C-KZG library on both gossip and RPC paths. No code path in the audited Go code allows cells with out-of-range field elements to be accepted. The findings from CHK-0062 (queue saturation DoS) are the relevant availability concern for this path, but do not constitute a violation of the field element range validation invariant. The absence of Go-level defense-in-depth is an informational finding only.
scope_filtering.severity_estimate: Informational (validation confirmed via C-KZG library on both paths)

audit_items.reasoning: Field element range validation for cells received via P2P gossip and RPC is correctly enforced by the C-KZG library within VerifyCellKZGProofBatch, which is called on both paths. Cells with bytes representing values >= BLS_MODULUS are rejected (ValidationReject for gossip, error for RPC). The gossip path has an orthogonal availability concern (CHK-0062, queue saturation DoS → ValidationIgnore) that does not compromise field element range validation correctness. Both gossip and RPC paths consistently apply the cryptographic range check. No code gap exists for this specific invariant.
recommendations: Add integration tests specifically for cells with V = BLS_MODULUS (exact boundary) and V = BLS_MODULUS+1 on both gossip and RPC paths to confirm C-KZG library behavior
Ensure peer scoring correctly penalizes peers that repeatedly send sidecars with out-of-range field elements (they should receive ValidationReject, triggering negative gossip score)
